# AI and Medicare: 3 steps to use technology to navigate the Annual Enrollment Period


*By **[Whitney Stidom](https://news.ehealthinsurance.com/experts/whitney-stidom)** , vice president of consumer enablement, **[eHealth](https://www.ehealthinsurance.com/)***


More Americans than ever are turning to artificial intelligence (AI) to compare everything from books to


banks to health benefits


. That includes Medicare plans, especially during the


fall’s


Annual Enrollment Period (Oct. 15 through Dec. 7).


In fact, new


**[eHealth research](https://news.ehealthinsurance.com/news/survey-half-of-medicare-beneficiaries-have-skipped-medical-care-in-the-past-year-due-to-confusion-over-their-coverage)** shows that


62% of Medicare beneficiaries who


intend


to review their


plans


for 2027


anticipate


us


ing


AI tools to help them compare


options


.


While AI can play a valuable role in the comparison-shopping process, it is important


that


Medicare beneficiaries understand th


e


technology’s


limitations — and the necessary steps to overcome them.


With a record number of Medicare beneficiaries


now


making


health plan


decisions


for next year, here are three steps to use AI effectively to compare plans and make


a


mo


re


informed decision based on individual needs and budgets.


**Step 1: Use AI to understand Medicare plan options and** **key insurance terms.**


Medicare is notoriously complex, with


[71% of beneficiaries](https://news.ehealthinsurance.com/news/survey-half-of-medicare-beneficiaries-have-skipped-medical-care-in-the-past-year-due-to-confusion-over-their-coverage) saying that shopping for a plan is confusing. AI


can help simplify Medicare,


in pa


rt


by


cla


rify


ing


basic


differences between Original Medicare, Medicare Supplement, Medicare Advantage and Medicare Part D


plans


.


It can also


c


la


rify


key Medicare


concepts


in


every-day


language, including terms such as premium, deductible, copay


,


coinsurance, and drug formularies.


Given how confusing these terms and concepts are for most Americans, AI can help Medicare beneficiaries become more knowledgeable when it comes to understanding how health insurance works


.


**Step 2: Use AI for initial plan research and to create an enrollment checklist.** AI can also help with


initial


Medicare plan research, including generating an enrollment checklist and


a


list of questions to ask yourself as you begin reviewing plans.


AI excels at helping you think through the pros and cons of different Medicare plan options, enabling you to contemplate the potential implications of different coverage decisions. With AI


aiding in


initial research and


helping you


to think through various plan options, it will be easier to understand and compare the Medicare options available in your area


.


**Step 3: Avoid using AI to make final decision s and don’t share personal information .** Most AI chatbots


don’t


have access to the latest Medicare plan information


, which often


changes


each year and


can


vary depending on where you live


. As a result,


AI may not always


provide


the most up-to-date answers


or reflect current plans, healthcare provider networks


,


or prescription drug formularies


.


It’s


also


wise to use caution when sharing personal or health information online


, so a


void


giving


consumer AI tools


sensitive information such as your Medicare


identification


number, Social Security number, or medical records.


Before choosing a plan, confirm plan costs,


healthcare


provider networks, prescription drug coverage, and eligibility through a trusted


government


site


, a


counselor with a S


tate


H


ealth


Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP)


or a licensed insurance agent.


While AI is a powerful resource, it is important to always


double-check


the information and guidance


it provides


.


With


AI becoming a bigger part of healthcare,


it’s


important


for


Medicare beneficiaries and their family members


to


use these resources


responsibly


, while


verify


ing


important coverage decisions


before enrolling


.


***[Whitney Stidom](https://news.ehealthinsurance.com/experts/whitney-stidom)** is vice president of consumer enablement at **[eHealth](http://www.ehealthinsurance.com/)** , an online health insurance marketplace that helps consumers navigate their health benefit decisions .*
